fda-trutakna-iga-nephropathy.name: FDA approves Trutakna for IgA nephropathy
fda-trutakna-iga-nephropathy.summary: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to Trutakna (atacicept-vymj) on 7 July 2026 to reduce protein in the urine in adults with primary IgA nephropathy.
keyPoints: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to Trutakna (atacicept-vymj) on 7 July 2026.
It is an injection for adults with primary IgA nephropathy at risk of disease progression.
The approval rests on a reduction in proteinuria; the FDA says it is not established whether the medicine slows kidney function decline.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 7 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Trutakna (atacicept-vymj), an injection given under the skin.

It is approved for adults with primary IgA nephropathy, a kidney disease, who are at risk of the disease getting worse.

The FDA describes it as the first approved medicine that targets both BAFF and APRIL, two signalling proteins involved in the survival and maturation of certain immune cells.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
Accelerated approval here rests on a reduction in proteinuria, which means protein in the urine.

The FDA states that it has not been established whether Trutakna slows the decline in kidney function over the long term, and that an ongoing trial must be completed to confirm this.

The efficacy and safety data come from a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves New Treatment to Reduce Proteinuria in Adults with Primary Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy

references.title: FDA Approves New Treatment to Reduce Proteinuria in Adults with Primary Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy

fda-hibsago-chronic-hepatitis-b.name: FDA approves Hibsago for chronic hepatitis B
fda-hibsago-chronic-hepatitis-b.summary: The US FDA approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) on 20 October 2026, the first antisense oligonucleotide approved for chronic hepatitis B in certain adults.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) on 20 October 2026.
The FDA calls it the first antisense oligonucleotide approved to treat chronic hepatitis B.
It is for certain adults without cirrhosis and is used alongside existing antiviral therapy.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 20 October 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) for chronic hepatitis B.

The FDA says it is the first approved antisense oligonucleotide for chronic hepatitis B.

It is approved for certain adults without cirrhosis, as an addition to existing antiviral therapy.

The FDA says eligible patients have taken antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed virus levels, and have a hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) level below a set threshold measured with an FDA-authorised test.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA reports that 24 weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19% of the patients who had received Hibsago still had the virus under control.

The FDA granted the medicine Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations, and its application received Priority Review.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment

references.title: FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment

fda-dostarlimab-rectal-cancer.name: FDA approves dostarlimab for rectal cancer
fda-dostarlimab-rectal-cancer.summary: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to dostarlimab (Jemperli) on 19 October 2026 for adults with certain locally advanced rectal cancers.
keyPoints: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to dostarlimab (Jemperli, GSK) on 19 October 2026.
It applies to adults with stage II or III locally advanced rectal cancer that is dMMR or MSI-H.
The approval rests on interim results from a single-arm, open-label study called AZUR-1.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 19 October 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to dostarlimab (Jemperli, GSK).

It is approved for adults with stage II or III locally advanced rectal cancer whose tumours are mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H).

The FDA says it acted four months ahead of its goal date, and that the drug had earlier received breakthrough therapy designation.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says the approval relied on interim results from AZUR-1, a single-arm, open-label study in patients with previously untreated dMMR or MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer.

Because the approval is accelerated, the sponsor must keep following patients to confirm lasting benefit.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to dostarlimab for locally advanced rectal cancer

fda-atezolizumab-stage-iii-colon-cancer.name: FDA approves atezolizumab for colon cancer
fda-atezolizumab-stage-iii-colon-cancer.summary: The US FDA approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq) with chemotherapy on 8 October 2026 as adjuvant treatment for stage III mismatch repair deficient colon cancer.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq) on 8 October 2026 for stage III dMMR colon cancer.
It is given with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin as adjuvant treatment.
The approval rests on a randomised, open-label trial called ATOMIC.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 8 October 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq, Genentech) with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin for adjuvant treatment of stage III mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colon cancer.

The approval covers adults and children aged two years and older.

A subcutaneous form, Tecentriq Hybreza, is approved with the same chemotherapy for patients aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA notes that ATOMIC enrolled 711 adults and one paediatric patient.

Adjuvant treatment is given after surgery to lower the chance of the cancer returning.

The FDA says the approval rests on the ATOMIC trial, a randomised, open-label, active-controlled study in people with stage III dMMR colon cancer after complete removal of the primary tumour.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA approves atezolizumab in combination with chemotherapy for Stage III mismatch repair deficient colon cancer

references.title: FDA approves atezolizumab in combination with chemotherapy for Stage III mismatch repair deficient colon cancer

fda-tucatinib-her2-breast-cancer-mainten.name: FDA approves tucatinib for HER2 breast cancer
fda-tucatinib-her2-breast-cancer-mainten.summary: The US FDA approved tucatinib (Tukysa) on 7 October 2026 with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as maintenance treatment for advanced HER2-positive breast cancer.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved tucatinib (Tukysa) on 7 October 2026.
It is used with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as maintenance treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer that is unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic.
The approved use follows induction therapy.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 7 October 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved tucatinib (Tukysa, Seagen, a subsidiary of Pfizer) in combination with trastuzumab and pertuzumab.

It is approved as maintenance treatment for adults with unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer that has been treated with induction therapy.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
In the trial, patients received tucatinib or placebo together with trastuzumab and pertuzumab.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA approves tucatinib with trastuzumab and pertuzumab for the maintenance treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer

fda-imlunestrant-abemaciclib-breast-canc.name: FDA approves imlunestrant with abemaciclib
fda-imlunestrant-abemaciclib-breast-canc.summary: The US FDA approved imlunestrant (Inluriyo) with abemaciclib on 18 September 2026 for ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced breast cancer.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved imlunestrant (Inluriyo) with abemaciclib (Verzenio) on 18 September 2026.
It applies to adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
The FDA also approved the Guardant360 CDx test to identify ESR1 mutations.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 18 September 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved imlunestrant (Inluriyo) in combination with abemaciclib (Verzenio).

The approval is for adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

The FDA also approved the Guardant360 CDx assay as a companion diagnostic to identify breast cancers with ESR1 mutations for treatment with imlunestrant and abemaciclib.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says the approval rests on the EMBER-3 trial, in which patients were randomly assigned to imlunestrant, standard endocrine therapy, or imlunestrant with abemaciclib.

The FDA had approved imlunestrant alone in September 2025 for ESR1-mutated disease that had progressed after at least one line of endocrine therapy.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

fda-injectafer-boxed-warning-low-phospha.name: FDA adds boxed warning to Injectafer
fda-injectafer-boxed-warning-low-phospha.summary: The US FDA said on 1 September 2026 that it added a boxed warning to Injectafer (ferric carboxymaltose) about the risk of low blood phosphate.
keyPoints: The US FDA added a boxed warning to Injectafer (ferric carboxymaltose) in a safety communication dated 1 September 2026.
The warning describes the risk of symptomatic hypophosphataemia, meaning low blood phosphate.
The FDA says reports continued despite earlier labelling changes in 2020 and 2023.
This is a US decision; UK availability and labelling are decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 1 September 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published a drug safety communication about ferric carboxymaltose injection, marketed as Injectafer.

The FDA says it approved label revisions that add a boxed warning, its most prominent safety warning.

The warning describes the risk of symptomatic hypophosphataemia, which is low phosphate in the blood.

It recommends phosphate monitoring in patients at risk and in any patient who receives a repeat course of treatment within three months of the previous course.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says symptomatic hypophosphataemia continued to be reported despite labelling changes in February 2020 and May 2023.

It also reports that, in data from its Sentinel System, serum phosphate testing took place in fewer than 20% of administration episodes.

Ferric carboxymaltose is an iron replacement given by injection into a vein.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Adds Boxed Warning to Labeling for Ferric Carboxymaltose Injection (Injectafer) to Describe Risk of Low Phosphate Levels

references.title: FDA Adds Boxed Warning to Labeling for Ferric Carboxymaltose Injection (Injectafer) to Describe Risk of Low Phosphate Levels

fda-generic-climara-pro-hormone-patch.name: FDA approves generic hormone therapy patch
fda-generic-climara-pro-hormone-patch.summary: The US FDA approved the first generic version of the Climara Pro once-weekly patch, which combines estradiol and levonorgestrel, on 20 October 2026.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved the first generic of Climara Pro on 20 October 2026.
Climara Pro is a once-weekly patch containing estradiol and levonorgestrel for women with an intact uterus.
The FDA describes the generic as therapeutically equivalent to the brand product.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 20 October 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first generic version of Climara Pro.

Climara Pro is a transdermal patch, worn for a week at a time, that contains estradiol and levonorgestrel and is for women with an intact uterus.

The FDA describes the generic as therapeutically equivalent to the brand product.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says the progestogen in the patch is there to reduce the risk of endometrial hyperplasia, which can occur with oestrogen alone.

The agency presented the approval as a way to widen access to medicines.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women

references.title: FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women

nih-extra-year-school-dementia-diagnoses.name: NIH-funded study links schooling to dementia
nih-extra-year-school-dementia-diagnoses.summary: An NIH-funded study reports that one extra year of secondary school in the UK was linked to fewer dementia diagnoses later in life, with the largest effect in people at higher genetic risk.
keyPoints: An NIH news release dated 23 October 2026 describes an NIH-funded study of schooling and dementia.
The study used a UK reform that raised the minimum school-leaving age by one year.
It reports fewer dementia diagnoses later in life, with the largest effect among people at higher genetic risk.
This is research news from a US agency, not UK guidance.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
A US National Institutes of Health (NIH) news release dated 23 October 2026 describes a study that found an extra year of secondary school was associated with fewer dementia diagnoses later in life.

The NIH funded the study, which was led by researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Southern California.

The researchers analysed a UK education reform that raised the minimum school-leaving age by one year, treating it as a natural experiment.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The release says the effect was largest among people at higher genetic risk of dementia.

The researchers estimated a reduction of 0.88 percentage points in Alzheimer's disease and related dementia over 50 years, which the release calls sizeable given how low overall dementia rates were in the study population.

The release notes that as the group ages, the gap between those who stayed in school and those who left may grow or shrink.

This is research news from a US agency; it does not change UK guidance.

source.title: An extra year of secondary school lowered dementia diagnoses later in life

references.title: An extra year of secondary school lowered dementia diagnoses later in life

fda-zidesamtinib-ros1-lung-cancer.name: FDA approves zidesamtinib for ROS1 lung cancer
fda-zidesamtinib-ros1-lung-cancer.summary: The US FDA approved zidesamtinib (Jideytro) on 22 July 2026 for adults with previously treated ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved zidesamtinib (Jideytro, Nuvalent) on 22 July 2026.
It is for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer who have had at least one ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
The approval rests on a single-arm, open-label trial called ARROS-1.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 22 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved zidesamtinib (Jideytro, Nuvalent).

It is approved for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer who have already received at least one ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says the approval rests on ARROS-1, a single-arm, open-label trial.

The FDA acted two months before its goal date, and the medicine holds orphan drug designation.

The label lists warnings that include central nervous system adverse reactions, QTc interval prolongation, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, skeletal fractures, and muscle pain with raised creatine phosphokinase.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA approves zidesamtinib for ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer

references.title: FDA approves zidesamtinib for ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer

fda-thyroid-tablets-lot-recall-vitruvias.name: US recall of one lot of thyroid tablets
fda-thyroid-tablets-lot-recall-vitruvias.summary: Vitruvias Therapeutics announced a US recall of one lot of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg on 21 August 2026 because of possible superpotency.
keyPoints: Vitruvias Therapeutics announced the recall on 21 August 2026 and the US FDA posted it on 24 August 2026.
It covers one lot, number 504950, of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg, because of possible superpotency.
The notice says too much thyroid hormone can cause symptoms of an overactive thyroid.
This is a US recall; UK medicines alerts come from the MHRA.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
Vitruvias Therapeutics announced on 21 August 2026 a nationwide recall in the US of one lot of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg, and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published the notice on 24 August 2026.

The recalled lot is number 504950, and the recall is to consumer level.

The reason given is that testing confirmed the product could be superpotent.

The notice says the company has received no reports of adverse events linked to the recall.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The notice says superpotent thyroid tablets can cause symptoms of an overactive thyroid, such as weight loss and changes in heart rate.

It describes older adults, pregnant women and infants as more vulnerable, especially with long-term use.

The notice says people currently using this lot should not stop without first talking to their healthcare provider, who can advise on next steps or a replacement prescription.

The FDA has said that animal-derived (desiccated) thyroid medicines are unapproved, meaning the agency has not reviewed them for safety, effectiveness or quality.

This is a US recall notice; any UK action on medicines is decided separately by the MHRA.

source.title: Vitruvias Therapeutics, Inc Issues Nationwide Recall of One Lot of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg Due to Potential Super Potency

references.title: Vitruvias Therapeutics, Inc Issues Nationwide Recall of One Lot of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg Due to Potential Super Potency

cdc-2026-2027-respiratory-season-outlook.name: CDC outlook for the 2026-27 respiratory season
cdc-2026-2027-respiratory-season-outlook.summary: The US CDC's outlook dated 23 September 2026 expects the peak of combined COVID-19, flu and RSV hospital admissions to be similar to last season, with low to moderate confidence.
keyPoints: The CDC published its 2026-2027 Respiratory Disease Season Outlook on 23 September 2026.
It expects the combined peak hospitalisation rate for COVID-19, influenza and RSV to be within 20% of the 2025-2026 peak.
The CDC calls the outlook high-level information, not a forecast, and says it may change.
This outlook describes the US, not the UK.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) published a 2026-2027 Respiratory Disease Season Outlook dated 23 September 2026.

The CDC describes it as high-level information on how the season could unfold, and says it is not a forecast.

It expects the peak combined hospitalisation rate for COVID-19, influenza and RSV to be within 20% of the 2025-2026 peak, with low to moderate confidence.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
For influenza, the CDC says there is no evidence that a high-severity season is more likely this year.

For RSV, it notes that the 2025-2026 peak came later than in earlier seasons and that the cause of the late peak is unclear.

The CDC lists a higher peak as a risk, driven by viruses that evade existing immunity or by lower vaccine uptake or effectiveness.

This outlook describes the US season; UK figures and vaccination advice come from UKHSA and the NHS.

source.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: 2026-2027 Respiratory Disease Season Outlook

fda-gedatolisib-hr-positive-breast-cance.name: FDA approves gedatolisib for breast cancer
fda-gedatolisib-hr-positive-breast-cance.summary: The US FDA approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) on 14 July 2026 with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, for certain HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancers.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk, Celcuity) on 14 July 2026.
It is used with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, in adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer without a detectable PIK3CA mutation.
The approval rests on the VIKTORIA-1 trial.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 14 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk, Celcuity) in combination with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib.

It is approved for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has no detectable PIK3CA mutation and has progressed after at least one line of endocrine therapy.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says efficacy was evaluated in VIKTORIA-1, an open-label study in which patients were randomly assigned to gedatolisib with fulvestrant and palbociclib, gedatolisib with fulvestrant, or fulvestrant alone.

The approval letter requires a further randomised trial to characterise known serious risks, including severe stomatitis and mucosal inflammation.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

nih-losartan-brown-fat-study.name: NIH-funded study: losartan and brown fat
nih-losartan-brown-fat-study.summary: An NIH-funded study reports that losartan, a blood pressure medicine, raised brown fat activity in mice and cells; the work is early-stage laboratory research.
keyPoints: An NIH news release dated 14 October 2026 describes an NIH-funded study of losartan and brown fat.
The researchers first linked brown fat to angiotensin receptor blockers by analysing patient data.
Losartan increased brown fat activity in mice and the metabolic activity of brown fat cells.
This is US research news, not UK guidance.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
A US National Institutes of Health (NIH) news release dated 14 October 2026 describes an NIH-funded study in which scientists found that losartan, a common blood pressure medicine, increased brown fat activity and boosted metabolism in mice.

The researchers first linked brown fat to the drug class called angiotensin receptor blockers by analysing data from more than 100,000 patients.

When they tested losartan directly on brown fat cells, it increased the cells' metabolic activity.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The findings come from patient data analysis and from experiments in mice and cells.

The lead author suggests the approach could stimulate brown fat even in people with normal blood pressure, although the experiments so far were in mice and cells.

This is research news from a US agency; it does not change UK guidance on blood pressure treatment.

source.title: A blood-pressure drug may activate health-promoting brown fat

references.title: A blood-pressure drug may activate health-promoting brown fat

fda-stelara-pediatric-ulcerative-colitis.name: FDA approves Stelara for children with colitis
fda-stelara-pediatric-ulcerative-colitis.summary: The US FDA approved Stelara (ustekinumab) for children aged 2 and older with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, in August 2026.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved Stelara (ustekinumab) injection for paediatric ulcerative colitis in August 2026.
It covers patients aged 2 years and older with moderately to severely active disease.
The FDA says Stelara is the first approved monoclonal antibody not targeting TNF alpha for the two main forms of paediatric inflammatory bowel disease.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Stelara (ustekinumab) injection for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in patients aged 2 years and older.

The FDA's orphan drug database lists the marketing approval date for this use as 28 August 2026.

The FDA says Stelara was approved on 15 April 2026 for moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in patients aged 2 years and older.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says Stelara is the first approved therapeutic monoclonal antibody that does not target TNF alpha for the two main forms of paediatric inflammatory bowel disease.

The FDA lists the most common adverse reactions in children with ulcerative colitis as nasopharyngitis (a common cold), headache, abdominal pain, influenza, fever, diarrhoea, sinusitis, fatigue and nausea.

Stelara has orphan drug designation for this use.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves Stelara for Pediatric Ulcerative Colitis

references.title: FDA Approves Stelara for Pediatric Ulcerative Colitis

fda-casgevy-sickle-cell-children-aged-2-.name: FDA approves gene therapy for young children
fda-casgevy-sickle-cell-children-aged-2-.summary: The US FDA approved Casgevy on 1 July 2026 for children aged 2 and older with sickle cell disease, which it calls the first gene therapy for this age group.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) for patients aged 2 years and older on 1 July 2026.
It covers sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
The FDA first approved Casgevy and Lyfgenia for sickle cell disease in December 2023, for patients aged 12 and older.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 1 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) for patients aged 2 years and older.

The FDA says it is the first gene therapy approved for patients aged 2 years and older with sickle cell disease.

The approval covers sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises, and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA first approved Casgevy and Lyfgenia for sickle cell disease in December 2023, for patients aged 12 and older.

The FDA notes that Casgevy is the first FDA-approved therapy that uses CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing.

Before the Casgevy infusion, patients receive a high-intensity preparatory treatment called myeloablative conditioning.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Young Children with Sickle Cell Disease

fda-ezplaz-freeze-dried-plasma-licensed.name: FDA licenses first freeze-dried plasma
fda-ezplaz-freeze-dried-plasma-licensed.summary: The US FDA licensed Ezplaz Freeze Dried Plasma on 29 July 2026, the first freeze-dried plasma product licensed in the US, for adults who need plasma.
keyPoints: The US FDA licensed Ezplaz Freeze Dried Plasma on 29 July 2026.
The FDA says it is the first freeze-dried plasma product licensed in the United States.
Its intended use is transfusion in adults who need plasma and for whom other plasma products are not available.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 29 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) licensed Ezplaz Freeze Dried Plasma, which it describes as the first freeze-dried plasma product licensed for use in the United States.

Its intended use is transfusion in adult patients who need plasma and for whom other plasma products are not available.

The FDA says Ezplaz is made from a single unit of fresh frozen plasma collected from FDA-licensed blood establishments.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
Each kit includes the freeze-dried plasma, a bag of sterile water and transfusion sets.

The licence went to Vascular Solutions, LLC, a subsidiary of Teleflex.

Before licensure the FDA had authorised a different product, French FDP, under an emergency use authorisation for military use; the FDA notes it is not an FDA-licensed product.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Licenses First-Ever Freeze-Dried Plasma Product in the U.S.

references.title: FDA Licenses First-Ever Freeze-Dried Plasma Product in the U.S.

fda-camzyos-children-obstructive-hcm.name: FDA approves Camzyos for children
fda-camzyos-children-obstructive-hcm.summary: The US FDA approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for children weighing at least 30 kg with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, on 30 September 2026.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for children weighing at least 30 kg with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on 30 September 2026.
The FDA says it is the first treatment to improve functional capacity and symptoms in children with this condition.
Camzyos carries a boxed warning for the risk of heart failure and is available only through a restricted programme.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 30 September 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for children weighing at least 30 kg with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

The FDA describes this as the first treatment to improve functional capacity and symptoms in children with the condition.

It describes the condition as inherited and causing a thickened heart muscle, with symptoms that can include shortness of breath, fatigue and an abnormal heart rhythm that can be life-threatening.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
In the paediatric study, patients were randomly assigned to Camzyos or placebo, and Camzyos reduced the Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract gradient compared with placebo.

The FDA says adult data showed a similar reduction, and that it expects the drug to help paediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.

Camzyos carries a boxed warning for the risk of heart failure and is available only through a restricted programme called the Camzyos Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS).

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.
